text.title: Roadmap Design Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding Roadmap Design. Each pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale; HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override. Rules r11–r19 fold in the former operational-rules file: Concrete rules for roadmap maintenance, audience publishing, and agent-specific gotchas.

rule.statement: Each roadmap item is an outcome statement, not a feature. Features sit beneath outcomes.
rule.rationale: Each roadmap item is an outcome statement, not a feature. Features sit beneath outcomes.

rule.statement: Use Now / Next / Later horizons; do not put dates on Next or Later.
rule.rationale: Use Now / Next / Later horizons; do not put dates on Next or Later.

rule.statement: Every item carries a confidence label (high/medium/low) tied to evidence held.
rule.rationale: Every item carries a confidence label (high/medium/low) tied to evidence held.

rule.statement: Roadmap reviewed quarterly; items can move between horizons or off.
rule.rationale: Roadmap reviewed quarterly; items can move between horizons or off.

rule.statement: Later items are bets, not commitments; copy must read that way.
rule.rationale: Later items are bets, not commitments; copy must read that way.

rule.statement: Select the format from the uncertainty level before applying r2: low → timeline (or Kanban when the audience is internal only); medium → Now/Next/Later; high → outcome-themed, or Now/Next/Later at theme level when it is shared externally. r2's horizon rules bind once Now/Next/Later is the selected format.
rule.rationale: Format mismatch is the root cause of roadmap trust failures — a timeline in a high-uncertainty context creates commitments that cannot be kept, and stakeholder trust dies on the first slip. Uncertainty and the external-sharing requirement pick the format; audience preference does not, because stakeholders always ask for dates. Original wording of the same rationale: Format mismatch is the root cause of roadmap trust failures. A timeline roadmap in a high-uncertainty context creates commitments that cannot be kept, destroying stakeholder trust on every slip. The format catalogue and selection matrix are in the section below.

rule.statement: Maintain one internal source-of-truth roadmap; emit every external view as a derivative of it — never copy-paste. Maintain two artefacts: internal roadmap (full detail: outcomes, owners, confidence, metrics) and external roadmap (themes and benefits only, no confidence levels, no owners, no metric targets). Sync via script, not copy-paste.
rule.rationale: Two hand-maintained copies diverge within one cycle, and the copy the customer holds is the one nobody re-checks. A derived view cannot drift from its source. Sharing confidence levels externally signals uncertainty in a way that customers interpret as incompetence. Sharing metric targets creates contractual expectations. Sharing owners exposes internal structure. Each audience needs a different abstraction level.

rule.statement: The external view names themes and benefits only — never specific metric targets, confidence labels, or owners.
rule.rationale: A published metric target is read as a commitment and creates contractual expectation; a published confidence label is read as incompetence. Each audience needs a different abstraction level.

rule.statement: Internal roadmap: monthly review. External roadmap: quarterly publish. Both cadences are named in the artefact, not left implicit.
rule.rationale: r4 fixes the review beat; this fixes the publish beat. A roadmap reviewed monthly but never republished leaves stakeholders reading a stale external view while the team believes it is current.

rule.statement: Every roadmap carries an explicit not-doing list at the horizon scope, each entry with a reason. Always include an "Explicitly Not Doing" section with reasons. It doubles as a future review log for stakeholder questions like "why didn't we build X?"
rule.rationale: Without stated exclusions every reasonable idea stays a candidate for this quarter. The list doubles as a review log that closes re-requests with a reference instead of reopening the debate. Stakeholders re-request excluded items constantly. A documented reason closes each request with a reference instead of reopening the debate. It also prevents reinventing the same prioritisation each quarter.

rule.statement: For a solo founder, the roadmap must fit on one screen. If it does not, it is a backlog with a roadmap header, not a roadmap.
rule.rationale: A roadmap communicates strategic direction. Anything requiring scrolling has too much detail for strategic communication and too little for task execution. It serves neither purpose.

rule.statement: Group all planned work into 3–5 themes. For each theme write: name, which objective it drives, why it is prioritised now, and 2–3 example initiatives. No theme should be orphaned from an objective.
rule.rationale: Themes without objectives are backlog categories, not strategic groupings. The objective link is what prevents "Later" from becoming a permanent graveyard of low-priority features.

rule.statement: Assign each initiative a confidence level: High (committed and scoped), Medium (planned, needs scoping), Low (exploring, tentative). At least 30% of items must be Medium or Low — if everything is High, the labelling is decoration.
rule.rationale: Uniform High confidence strips the signal from Now-Next-Later. Stakeholders learn to ignore confidence levels that are never Low, and the roadmap loses its communication function. Extends r3-confidence-labels with the distribution floor.

rule.statement: Limit Now to 5 initiatives maximum. Past 5, the team is effectively planning a backlog sprint, not a strategic now-horizon.
rule.rationale: Teams can execute 3–5 significant initiatives in parallel before coordination costs outweigh benefits. More than 5 in Now signals that priorities have not been made.

rule.statement: For each horizon, document: why you chose these initiatives, what you are NOT doing and why, dependencies and risks, and how success will be measured. The "not doing" section is mandatory — it stops scope creep better than any priority list.
rule.rationale: Without explicit exclusions, every reasonable idea becomes a candidate for this quarter. The not-doing list also creates a retrospective record of scope decisions, which is invaluable for explaining past trade-offs. Extends r10-not-doing-list with the other three context fields.

rule.statement: Every initiative must link to one objective ID. Initiatives without an objective link are strategy leakage — remove them or create the missing objective.
rule.rationale: Orphaned initiatives represent work that is in the plan without strategic justification. They accumulate over time and eventually dominate the roadmap without anyone being able to explain why.

rule.statement: Update cadence: monthly review of the solution list, quarterly rewrite of the full document. Never rewrite the whole doc each sprint — that destroys the historical diff signal.
rule.rationale: Quarter-to-quarter diffs are the primary retrospective artefact. Frequent complete rewrites make it impossible to see how the plan evolved or why certain items moved. Same beats as r9-publish-cadence; this rule adds the prohibition on per-sprint rewrites.

rule.statement: Never let an agent ship the external roadmap without human review. Review for commitments, NDAs, and competitive signalling — LLMs cannot assess business risk context.
rule.rationale: External roadmaps are marketing documents with legal and competitive implications. An LLM cannot assess NDA scope, competitive sensitivity, or contractual interpretation. Human checkpoint is mandatory before publication.

rule.statement: When prompting an LLM for roadmap generation: force confidence distribution (now=mostly High, next=mostly Medium, later=mostly Low), cap themes at 3–5, cap Now initiatives at 5, mark not_doing as a required field. When the LLM is fed a previous quarter's roadmap as context, explicitly instruct it to identify what changed since the last review — otherwise it will simply restate the prior roadmap.
rule.rationale: LLMs default to "everything is High confidence", produce 8+ themes, and silently drop the not-doing column because it produces no generative content. Explicit constraints in the prompt override these defaults. Models are trained to be helpful, which defaults to continuity. Without explicit change-detection instructions, the agent produces a cosmetically different version of the same document.

rule.statement: If preconditions in AGENTS.md "Applies If" do not all hold, OR any "Skip If" disqualifier is true, do not run this methodology — route to the named alternative.
rule.rationale: Methodologies are pre-condition gated; running them out-of-scope produces noise and burns the agent context budget.

rule.statement: If preconditions hold, execute the procedure in `content/04-procedure.xml` (or the rule set above when complexity is light), emit the artefact specified by `content/02-output-contract.xml`, and validate with `scripts/validate-roadmap-design.py` before returning.
rule.rationale: Tying the entry rule to the validator script closes the loop between policy and machine check.

section.title: Format catalogue and selection matrix
section.p: Four roadmap types with a selection matrix based on uncertainty, external-sharing needs, commitment level, and team maturity. Rule r6-format-by-uncertainty is the single rule that applies this matrix.

list.item: Timeline roadmap: date-based, quarters or months, committed work. Use when: external sharing required with committed deliverables, low uncertainty, high team maturity.
Now-Next-Later roadmap: priority sequence, no dates. Use when: internal or limited external sharing, medium uncertainty, any team maturity.
Outcome-based roadmap: metric targets per theme. Use when: strategic alignment focus, high uncertainty, external sharing acceptable at theme level.
Kanban roadmap: live work state. Use when: internal teams only, pure execution visibility, no strategic communication needed.

section.p: Choose the format by uncertainty level first, then external-sharing requirement. High uncertainty + external sharing = outcome-based or Now-Next-Later (themes only). Low uncertainty + external sharing = timeline.

list.item: External sharing required: timeline (committed) or outcome/Now-Next-Later (theme level only)
